6 Minute English now comes with a video🤩 ! It's the same programme that you know and love 💖, but now you can see us! 👀 Let us know what you think in the comments.
Anyone who has had their heart broken will know how horrible it feels. But did you know that the pain you feel is not just imaginary – it registers in the same part of the brain that processes physical pain. So, why do we feel this pain? And if it feels so bad, what is the point of being in love in the first place? Neil and Georgie discuss this and teach you some new vocabulary.

lessons.title: Stop making these apostrophe mistakes – a Mini English Lesson
lessons.desc:
The cat chased it’s tail. Can you spot the mistake?
Apostrophes have a habit of turning up where they don’t belong. Even confident English writers get them wrong, especially in plurals, possessive pronouns and the famous its/it’s problem.
In this Mini English Lesson, Zina shows you three common mistakes to avoid and a quick check that can save you every time.
Watch, then tell us in the comments if you ever make these mistakes!
Learn English online with the world’s English experts: https://learnenglish.pub/EnglishOnlineYT

lessons.title: Stop confusing these English words – a Mini English Lesson
lessons.desc:
Some English words are so close in sound, spelling or meaning that it can be easy to choose the wrong one without noticing. In your head, the sentence sounds fine. It’s just not what you meant to say.
In this Mini English Lesson, Jo takes on some of the most commonly confused words that can trip you up before you even realise it. Watch now to make sure the next word out of your mouth is the right one!
Learn English online with the world’s English experts: https://learnenglish.pub/EnglishOnlineYT

lessons.title: This is English: Where every accent belongs
lessons.desc:
'An accent isn't something to be corrected — it's a record of where you're from, who you are, and where you belong, and no accent is inherently better than any other.'
To mark English Language Day, Neil is joined by Rob Drummond, Professor of Sociolinguistics at Manchester Metropolitan University. Together, they explore This is English, a new British Council project about accent diversity across the UK and beyond. Find out more here: https://learnenglish.pub/ThisIsEnglishYT
We want to hear from you too — your stories, your experiences and your questions about accents.
Share in the comments.
